recipes.name: Follow-up email
recipes.instruction:
Write the follow-up email the requester can send after this meeting. The first paragraph is `Subject: ` and a short, specific subject. Then a greeting to the person in the `recipient` choice (write `[need: recipient name]` if none was given), a line of thanks, a short recap of what was discussed, and a list of what each side agreed, each item with its owner, taken from the action items and decisions. Give a next step and a date only if the meeting set them; otherwise write `[need: next step date]`. Match the `tone` choice (friendly or formal). Never promise a price, a delivery date, a discount or a term that is not in the meeting or the brief.

Use only the meeting material you are given (the transcript, notes, decisions, tasks and open questions) and the team brief when one is given. Never invent a name, number, date, price, commitment or answer. Where a fact you need is not there, write a blank such as `[need: <what is missing>]` instead of guessing.

recipes.name: Proposal
recipes.instruction:
Write a client proposal from this meeting and the brief, with these headings in order: Background; What we heard; Proposed solution; Scope and deliverables; Timeline; Investment; Terms and assumptions; Next steps. Timeline is a table (columns: Phase, What happens, When). Investment is a table (columns: Item, Price). What we heard comes from the transcript and notes. Prices, rates and terms come only from the brief or from what was said in the meeting; where neither states one, write a blank such as `[need: price for <item>]`. Name the client from the `recipient` choice, or `[need: client name]`. Match the `tone` choice.

Use only the meeting material you are given (the transcript, notes, decisions, tasks and open questions) and the team brief when one is given. Never invent a name, number, date, price, commitment or answer. Where a fact you need is not there, write a blank such as `[need: <what is missing>]` instead of guessing.

recipes.name: Requirements document
recipes.instruction:
Write a requirements document from this meeting with these headings in order: Goals; Users; Requirements; Open questions; Out of scope; Risks; Acceptance. Requirements is a table (columns: Requirement, Priority, Owner); fill Priority and Owner only when the meeting said them, else `[need: priority]` or `[need: owner]`. Open questions come from the open questions and from anything left undecided. Acceptance lists how the team said it will know the work is done, or `[need: acceptance criteria]`.

Use only the meeting material you are given (the transcript, notes, decisions, tasks and open questions) and the team brief when one is given. Never invent a name, number, date, price, commitment or answer. Where a fact you need is not there, write a blank such as `[need: <what is missing>]` instead of guessing.

recipes.name: Marketing post
recipes.instruction:
Write a post (a LinkedIn post or a short blog draft) from this product or customer meeting, for the audience in the `audience` choice (write for a general reader if none was given) and of the length in the `length` choice. Start with a hook, then the story or the point, then one call to action. Make no claim, statistic or customer quote that is not in the meeting or the brief. Name a customer or a person only if the meeting or the brief clearly allows it; otherwise write `[need: customer name]`.

Use only the meeting material you are given (the transcript, notes, decisions, tasks and open questions) and the team brief when one is given. Never invent a name, number, date, price, commitment or answer. Where a fact you need is not there, write a blank such as `[need: <what is missing>]` instead of guessing.

recipes.name: Decision memo
recipes.instruction:
Write a decision memo built from the decisions recorded for this meeting, with these headings in order: Context; Options discussed; The decision; Who decided; Consequences; Follow-ups. Take the decision and who made it from the decisions and the transcript. List only the options that were actually discussed. Follow-ups come from the action items, with owners.

Use only the meeting material you are given (the transcript, notes, decisions, tasks and open questions) and the team brief when one is given. Never invent a name, number, date, price, commitment or answer. Where a fact you need is not there, write a blank such as `[need: <what is missing>]` instead of guessing.

recipes.name: SOP / how-to
recipes.instruction:
Turn this walkthrough meeting into a standard operating procedure with these headings in order: Purpose; Before you start; Steps; Checks; Who does what. Steps is a numbered sequence in the order they were explained, one action each, naming the owner where the meeting did. Checks are how someone confirms a step worked, only where the meeting said so. Do not add steps that were not explained.

Use only the meeting material you are given (the transcript, notes, decisions, tasks and open questions) and the team brief when one is given. Never invent a name, number, date, price, commitment or answer. Where a fact you need is not there, write a blank such as `[need: <what is missing>]` instead of guessing.

recipes.name: Action tracker
recipes.instruction:
Make one table of the meeting's action items from its tasks, with the columns Task, Owner, Due date and Status, one row per task, in the order of the tasks. Copy the task wording. Owner, due date and status come only from the task; where one is not shown write `[need: owner]`, `[need: due date]` or `[need: status]`. Write a due date exactly as the task gives it.

Use only the meeting material you are given (the transcript, notes, decisions, tasks and open questions) and the team brief when one is given. Never invent a name, number, date, price, commitment or answer. Where a fact you need is not there, write a blank such as `[need: <what is missing>]` instead of guessing.

recipes.name: Board
recipes.instruction:
Make a one-page board of this meeting. Group the decisions, action items, open questions and key points into between three and six themes, one column per theme with a short heading. Each card is one decision, action, question or note in plain words, with its owner when the meeting names one, and the line it came from. Do not repeat a card.

Use only the meeting material you are given (the transcript, notes, decisions, tasks and open questions) and the team brief when one is given. Never invent a name, number, date, price, commitment or answer. Where a fact you need is not there, write a blank such as `[need: <what is missing>]` instead of guessing.

recipes.name: Status report
recipes.instruction:
Write a status report over the meetings you are given, with these headings in order: Progress; Decisions; Blockers; Next steps. Progress says what was done, taken from the notes and tasks, by meeting. Decisions is a table (columns: Decision, Meeting). Blockers and Next steps are bullet lists with owners where known. Say what each meeting recorded; give no percent complete and no forecast the meetings did not state.

Use only the meeting material you are given (the transcript, notes, decisions, tasks and open questions) and the team brief when one is given. Never invent a name, number, date, price, commitment or answer. Where a fact you need is not there, write a blank such as `[need: <what is missing>]` instead of guessing.

recipes.name: Client briefing
recipes.instruction:
Write a briefing for the next call with the same client, from the earlier meetings you are given, with these headings in order: History; What we promised; Open items; Questions to ask. History is short and in date order. What we promised lists only commitments the meetings record, with who made them. Open items come from the open tasks and open questions. Questions to ask are things the meetings left unresolved.

Use only the meeting material you are given (the transcript, notes, decisions, tasks and open questions) and the team brief when one is given. Never invent a name, number, date, price, commitment or answer. Where a fact you need is not there, write a blank such as `[need: <what is missing>]` instead of guessing.

recipes.name: Study guide
recipes.instruction:
Write a study guide from this class, in the order it was taught, with these headings: Key ideas; Definitions; Worked examples; What to revise. Give each definition as the lecturer gave it and each example as it was worked in class. Add nothing from a textbook or general knowledge. What to revise lists what the lecturer said to focus on, or the points that took the longest, each with the line it came from.

Use only the meeting material you are given (the transcript, notes, decisions, tasks and open questions) and the team brief when one is given. recipes.instruction:

If the `until` choice is not given, write `[need: exam date]` and give the order without dates. Never work out a calendar date.
